note: Trace form (research/trace-harness.md) for L11, run on L11's own twins ("twins": "..") with no warm-up route: neither trace.json nor the twins' erlang.config.json names one, so before each start's first requests the harness requests a path that does not exist and expects a 404 (the fallback). That warms the framework (the HTTP parser, Express's first dispatch) but not the database driver, and the report says so. Everything else is the L11 trace form's: its seed, schema, lockfile and overlay (the postcode file, the PDF module, the country count), with this form's entry, which leaves out the warm-up route. Each start is a fresh process: the fallback request, then every route's first request and the five after it, in an order rotated by one each start; a route whose first-request extra is at least three times the 404 request's own time in the same process and 20 ms above it, in every start, waits for set-up (STB-10). The 404's time is the baseline here, not the cheapest route's extra: with no route warmed that extra can be 0, and the bar would fall to 20 ms alone (CI run 44669987055: the clean twin's POST /orders cleared once in five starts, 24 ms against 0). A timing, judged under the relative timing rule (docs/decisions.md, Q8): a finding when every start clears the bar, none when no start does, and info (timing unreliable) for a mix; spread and load average are recorded only. defects are what the planted twin must report and the clean twin must not; every other request is a decoy, in both twins.
